issues.legal_issue: A watan consisting only of land revenue, rather than the soil, qualifies its holder for compensation upon resumption under the applicable abolition law.
material_facts: The holder claimed compensation for resumed watan lands, and the claim depended on whether the watan was of land revenue or of the soil.
The sanad used the word “lands” and had been issued following an inquiry under a law defining “land” to include a share of land revenue.
Contemporaneous alienation-register entries, earlier documents, and the treatment of the grant by revenue officers supported the conclusion that it was a grant of land revenue, not the soil.
issues.conclusion: The watan was a watan of land revenue only, so the holder was entitled to compensation under section 6(2); the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(2) of the Bombay Paragana and Kulkarni Watans (Abolition) Act, 1950 provides compensation for resumption where the watan is of land revenue. In construing the sanad, the Court applied the definition of “land” in Bombay Act II of 1863, which includes a share of land revenue, because the sanad was apparently issued pursuant to an inquiry under that Act. The word “lands” alone does not establish a grant of the soil; the Court considered the sanad in context and alongside contemporaneous register entries, earlier documents, and the consistent treatment by revenue officers. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.proceeding_is_resumption_compensation_cl: The proceeding seeks compensation for the resumption of a watan.
predicates.watan_was_land_revenue_only: The holder's watan consisted of a grant of land revenue and not a grant of the soil.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks compensation for resumption of a watan and the watan consisted only of land revenue, the holder is entitled to compensation for the resumption.
